chapter: Moving, Columbia Missouri and leaving home
title: Born at the end of World War I; how the times shape the music
summary: Thompson says people like the music of their times, links his birth in 1918 to a postwar wish for peace, and says beauty came out of ghetto surroundings.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: Yes. And of course styles change, so that possibly today the -- or in recent years the beauty hasn't perhaps been considered as paramount as well, free development and perhaps exploration and so on. But they're phases, probably. How do you feel?

Oh, yes, we could go into that. I think perhaps if we picked a later time in this discussion to talk about that. But it's true, I mean it's just like the earlier period when I was a little boy, which I was born at the end of World War, you know, 1918. Well, during that period when I was a kid, and after later became interested in music, was a period when they had all those crazy songs, you know, like the Charleston and all that stuff, and the ca

crazy dances and all that, and so forth. And they had the same (unintelligible) because of the war times, the times that we live in has to do with the basic music that people appreciate because of what they hear most of, you see.
And that is the situation today, comparative to the period when they had the great war, when I was a child. You know, it was just considered the -- is that World War I?

But as I said, I -- that's something else that may be significant in my life as well as many other people who were born during that period. I was born at the end of the war, which would be at the beginning of the rehabilitation of the human race all over the world.
Which is significant in my life.

Because I was a part of a beginning of people wanting to come back to natural, coming back to normal, of loving each other instead of fighting each other. And this was the general period of my life that was important during the period that I decided to become a musician. And which had a lot to do with my wanting to be a musician, because as I said, being complimented by people who liked my music, and

being loved by those people, who liked music, it made me produce music with a happy feeling. And I would like to feel that if I am producing music of beauty and feeling and expression, that it has been done because of those early surroundings I had in the midst of all of this oppression, and ghetto areas, and submission into back alleys and --
You know? Through all that has come some beauty out of me, you know.
